issue.title: Ansible Provisioner: Support Guidelines for ansible-playbook options

repository.name: vagrant
repository.description: Vagrant is a tool for building and distributing development environments.

issue.body:
With current open issues like
- #2103 (running ansible-playbook on the guest machine)
- #2924 (support of interactive prompts)
- #3241 / #3338 (support of vault options)
- #3431 (include vagrant default SSH identity into generated inventory)
- Why not deprecate/drop "official support" of `paramiko` mode? 
  - #3900: tricky to be potentially ready for smart mode (aka paramiko or ssh)
  - `ssh` is needed by #4071, ssh-forwarding, multiple ssh identities
  - smart mode corresponds to `ssh` in a large majority of vagrant setups
- support of new options introduced in Ansible 1.5.x (e.g. `--su-user`)

I think it is now necessary to clarify what the Ansible provisioner can/should offer, according to following facts:
- With Host-based provisioning, people might want to manually execute `ansible-playbook` or `ansible` commands against the Vagrant VMs.
- Guest-based provisioning cannot support interactive prompts (in Vagrant 1.x at least)
- Provisioner Advanced/Expert modes are not necessarily supported (especially if the integration is difficult to implement or use)
- `ansible.raw_arguments`, `ansible.raw_ssh_args` and an Ansible configuration file (e.g. local `ansible.cfg`) can be easily used to customize a lot of things.

The idea is here to establish a simple check-list to take decision about adding (or removing) support of provisioner options, being at maximum "user friendly and backward compatible". Feel free to bring your thoughts!

body: I was able to resolve via `raw_ssh_args`, I'll try and throw a gist together shortly.
I managed to narrow this down a bit further, here's a gist that can reproduce: https://gist.github.com/glenjamin/7f1d4335e7a9760b75e5

@glenjamin Thanks a lot for the excellent problem report, which was very easy to reproduce!

I think that in a Vagrant context, it is important to be able to ignore ssh `known_hosts` files (with opt-in / opt-out choice, of course).

As you mentioned, having `-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no` allows to keep going when the host key has changed, but running with an outdated entry in `known_hosts` silently leads to this nasty problem. For that kind of reasons, it seems that relaxing together both SSH settings is a good choice, as illustrated by `vagrant ssh-config` itself or `~/.ssh/config` example like:

```
Host 127.0.0.1
  StrictHostKeyChecking no
  UserKnownHostsFile /dev/null
```

The vagrant ansible provisioner currently uses `ANSIBLE_HOST_KEY_CHECKING` option (which is supported by both connection types `ssh` and `paramiko`), to control `StrictHostKeyChecking` when using native ssh connection. But there is currently no Ansible setting to control `UserKnownHostsFile` option, except via `ANSIBLE_SSH_ARGS` / ssh_args (see also the comments in ansible/ansible#3694).

Adding a new option to the Vagrant Ansible provisioner does not sound very good to me, so one possible _solution_ could be to force `-o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null` when `ansible.host_key_checking` is disabled and `--connection=ssh` is enabled (or maybe only if `config.ssh.forward_agent` is enabled). But I don't like very much the idea to mix these two options across `ANSIBLE_HOST_KEY_CHECKING` and `ANSIBLE_SSH_ARGS` parameters...

Before proceeding, I also think it is worth to verify with the Ansible project if there is a more general need to set `UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null` (I searched a bit across Github issues and the mailing list, but I didn't find concrete feature request so far).

@glenjamin @mitchellh thoughts?

issue.title: ssh-agent forwarding and `sudo: yes`

repository.name: ansible
repository.description: Ansible is a radically simple IT automation platform that makes your applications and systems easier to deploy and maintain. Automate everything from code deployment to network configuration to cloud management, in a language that approaches plain English, using SSH, with no agents to install on remote systems. https://docs.ansible.com.

issue.body:
##### Issue Type:

Bug Report
##### Ansible Version:

ansible 1.5.4
##### Environment:

Both Ubuntu 14.04, 64bit
##### Summary:

Ansible documentation promotes the use of ssh-agent, which's a great tool, but there are some issues when using it with `ForwardAgent`: a `sudo: yes` statement discards the environment variables, and thus agent forwarding is not functioning.

This can be tweaked with `sudo_flags=-HE` in the config, but when a subsequent `sudo: yes` occurs (e.g. in a contributed role) -- the environment is still discarded.

I believe that Ansible should really take care about ssh-agent so users don't have to experiment with dark hackery, shouldn't it?
##### Steps To Reproduce:

``` console
$ ssh-agent bash
$ ssh-add ~/.id_rsa

$ ssh -T git@github.com
Hi kolypto! You've successfully authenticated, 
but GitHub does not provide shell access.

$ ansible-playbook -K site.yml
```

site.yml:

``` yaml

---

- hosts: all
  sudo: yes
  tasks:
    - command: ssh 
             -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no 
             -T git@github.com
```
##### Expected Results:

> stderr: Hi kolypto! You've successfully authenticated, 
> but GitHub does not provide shell access.
##### Actual Results:

> stderr: Permission denied (publickey).

body: I've hit something similar too - I think the egregious part is that it happens silently and you don't realize exactly what is going on until after printing out a ton of debug info, and solving that would at least nudge the user in the right direction.

> I've hit something similar too

@makmanalp Thanks for reporting your bad experience. From https://gist.github.com/makmanalp/a95aa39f4b3171baeb5b (via ansible/ansible#7235), I suppose that you hit this issue after that your guest vm key changed. I'd like to solve this the better way possible, so could you please give us a few more details about your own case (gists are always welcome if it strongly differs from @glenjamin report):
- Are you also using SSH forwarding (`config.ssh.forward_agent = true` or setting `-o ForwardAgent=yes` somewhere in your config) ?
- Could you solve your problem with [ansible.raw_ssh_args = ["-o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null"]](https://gist.github.com/glenjamin/7f1d4335e7a9760b75e5#file-vagrantfile-L12-L13) workaround ?

@gildegoma Thank you for looking into it! I am using forwarding, and the solution was to just get rid of the old key. I'll try to reproduce tonight, but I think it's like you said, the VM key changed. I think that might have happened possibly because I did `vagrant destroy` and `vagrant up`. I'll post an update in a few hours.

After further investigation, here are the current Ansible configuration capabilities:
- Ansible 1.3+ provides [ANSIBLE_PARAMIKO_RECORD_HOST_KEYS](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/commit/cf6e1f8db915e763b2fa5e29186b558a55cd8733) option to skip writing into known hosts file (e.g. `~/.ssh/known_hosts`)
- Adding an option in Ansible to set `UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null` when using `ssh` connection was discussed in https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/3694#issuecomment-22530734, but it does not seem to be planned at the moment.

I've just opened a [discussion in Ansible Development Mailing List](https://groups.google.com/d/msg/ansible-devel/iuoZs1oImNs/6xrj5oa1CmoJ) to first ask if Ansible itself should provide an option to skip writing to `~/.ssh/known_hosts` file. If this is accepted, future versions of Vagrant will use Ansible proper settings. Otherwise we'll update the Ansible provisioner to potentially configure both connection modes (Paramiko and OpenSSH) so that `~/.ssh/known_hosts` is not modified, nor considered.

After discussing it, the Ansible team is not interested (for now) to introduce a new option to be able to skip the user known host file in a unified manner for `paramiko` and `ssh` connection modes. 

Therefore, we must rely on the existing options described above, which is far from ideal, but doable. Please note that I am not sure to find time before August to work on this. Pull request welcome, of course!
